extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting datasets/benchmarks to NeurIPS 2025 D&B track and the track's reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks call for papers
extracted.subtask_description: The NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks track call for papers describes the specific scope and review criteria for D&B submissions, including stringent hosting, accessibility, code, and metadata requirements (Croissant), and clarifies what kinds of dataset, benchmark, and tool contributions are in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equally stringent review as the main conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will be published in the NeurIPS proceedings and presented at the conference alongside the main track papers. As such, we aim for an equally stringent review as in the main conference track, while also allowing for track-specific guidelines, which we introduce below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The D&B track explicitly holds itself to the same review-stringency bar as the main NeurIPS track, with only the track-specific guidelines below being different.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind submissions allowed (anonymization optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets are often not possible to be reviewed in a double-blind fashion, and hence full anonymization will not be required for D&B paper submissions. Submissions to this track will be reviewed according to a set of criteria and best practices specifically designed for datasets and benchmarks, as described below. Authors can choose to submit either single-blind or double-blind. If it is possible to properly review the submission double-blind, i.e., if reviewers do not need access to non-anonymous repositories to review the work, then authors can also choose to submit the work anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymization is optional: single-blind is the default given that datasets often require non-anonymous repositories, but double-blind is allowed when review can be done without access to non-anonymous resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: No collusion permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS does not tolerate any collusion whereby authors secretly cooperate with reviewers, ACs, or SACs to obtain favorable reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on any form of collusion between authors and reviewers/ACs/SACs aimed at obtaining favourable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset hosting on dedicated ML platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: New datasets should be hosted at one of the hosting sites dedicated to ML datasets (Dataverse, Kaggle, Hugging Face, or OpenML) or at a bespoke hosting site if the dataset requires it. See the guidelines for data hosting for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets must be hosted at recognized ML data sites (Dataverse, Kaggle, Hugging Face, OpenML) or a justified bespoke site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code must be accessible and executable
rubrics_metrics.description: Code should be made accessible in an executable format via a hosting platform (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket). See the main track code guidelines for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code must be hosted on a platform like GitHub/Bitbucket and provided in an executable form, following the main track's code guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access available to all reviewers/ACs/SACs at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets and code should be available and accessible to all reviewers, ACs and SACs at the time of submission. Data should be found and obtained without a personal request to the PI. Code should be documented and executable. Non-compliance justifies the desk rejection of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At submission time, datasets and code must be obtainable without personal requests, and the code must be documented and executable; non-compliance is grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Croissant machine-readable metadata required
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use the Croissant machine-readable format to document their datasets in a machine-readable way and include the Croissant file with their paper submission in OpenReview. If your data is hosted on one of the dedicated ML data hosting sites (Kaggle, OpenML, Hugging Face, Dataverse) a Croissant metadata file is automatically generated for you. If you choose to host your data on a different hosting site you need to generate the Croissant metadata file yourself. You can verify the validity of your Croissant file via this online tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Croissant metadata files are mandatory for all D&B submissions; auto-generated on the dedicated platforms, otherwise authored manually and validated via the provided tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability by camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: All accepted papers should have their code and datasets documented and publicly available by the camera-ready deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By the camera-ready deadline, all accepted papers must have publicly available, documented code and datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data-centric ML research that enables or accelerates ML
rubrics_metrics.description: The NeurIPS 2025 D&B track welcomes all work on data-centric machine learning research (DMLR) that enable or accelerate ML research, covering ML datasets and benchmarks as well as algorithms, tools, methods, and analyses for working with ML data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope is explicitly broad: any data-centric work (datasets, benchmarks, algorithms, tools, methods, analyses) that enables or accelerates ML research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source libraries and tools in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&B track is proud to support the open source movement by encouraging submissions of open-source libraries and tools that enable or accelerate ML research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-source libraries and tools that enable/accelerate ML research are explicitly welcomed as in-scope submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: New datasets and carefully designed dataset collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope includes but is not limited to: New datasets, or carefully and thoughtfully designed (collections of) datasets based on previously available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both genuinely new datasets and 'carefully and thoughtfully designed' collections derived from existing data are in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data generators and RL environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Data generators and reinforcement learning environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data generators and RL environments are explicitly listed as in-scope contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-centric AI methods and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Data-centric AI methods and tools, e.g. to measure and improve data quality or utility, or studies in data-centric AI that bring important new insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods/tools that measure or improve data quality/utility, or data-centric studies offering new insight, are in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced collection/curation practices even without shareable data
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced practices in data collection and curation that are of general interest even if the data itself cannot be shared. Private data sets, however, cannot be listed as contributions, and the methodology should also be validated on reproducible and publicly available data/tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology papers are accepted even when the underlying private data cannot be shared, but the private dataset itself cannot be claimed as a contribution and methods must also be validated on public, reproducible data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible-development frameworks and dataset audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Frameworks for responsible dataset development, audits of existing datasets, identifying significant problems with existing datasets and their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible development frameworks, dataset audits, and critical analyses identifying problems with existing datasets are in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks and benchmarking methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks on new or existing datasets, as well as benchmarking tools, including novel benchmarking methodologies and designs, e.g., approaches to mitigate LLM contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes benchmarks on new/existing data, benchmarking tools, and methodological innovations such as LLM-contamination mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyses of ML challenges/competitions yielding new insight
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth analyses of machine learning challenges and competitions (by organisers and/or participants) that yield important new insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-hoc analyses of ML competitions are welcome if they deliver important new insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic analyses of existing systems on novel datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic analyses of existing systems on novel datasets yielding important new insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic evaluations of existing systems are in scope when applied to novel datasets and yielding new insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition papers held to same review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite competition papers from prior NeurIPS competitions to be submitted at the Datasets and Benchmarks track. They will not be given any special reviewing policy, and will be reviewed with the same requirements, standards as all other track submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior NeurIPS competition papers are welcome but receive no review-policy concessions; they are held to the same standards as other D&B submissions.
